docs.title: Welcome
docs.text: This site will contain various crafts and methods that focus on minimizing the ecological, humanitarian and economical impact. It'll include materials you can collect from nature, somewhat easily scavenge from trash and things you can easily find in stores.

docs.title: Iron Acetate
docs.text: Iron acetate is a great mordant for fabrics and can be used to color wood.

docs.title: How to make
docs.text: Collect some rusty iron and put it in a non-metallic jar. Add vinegar, preferably enough to cover the iron. Put on a cloth over the opening of the jar and put a rubber band around it. Let sit for a few weeks.

docs.title: Important notes
docs.text: Do not seal the jar. The process creates pressure that needs to be able to come out.

docs.title: Uses
docs.text:
As a mordant. Saddener. Binds well.

As a Wood Stain.

docs.title: Iron Acetate
docs.text: Colors woods in different colors depending on wood type.
